title: Yan two-session browser-window vs iframe resource benchmark

result.runtime_memory_metric: Median proportional set size (PSS) across the Chromium process tree, KiB; each trial sampled 12 times after warm-up.

method.comparison: Two separate Chromium windows, each with one Yan conversation, versus one Yan page with one active iframe pane; exactly two synthetic idle conversations in both modes.
method.browser_environment: Headless Chromium 156.0.8078.47 on Debian GNU/Linux 12; 1920x1080 viewport; same local server and browser build; fresh browser profile for each trial; modes alternated across six trials.
method.model_activity: None; no model requests or generated replies.
method.browser_profile_growth_definition: Bytes added to the fresh browser profile relative to its blank-browser baseline during a trial. This is browser-profile growth, not installed application size or a clean measurement of app-only disk use.
method.functional_check_definition: For each of the two conversations, verify its expected content rendered and its input was enabled. No typing, sending, response streaming, or subjective usability rating was measured.

interpretation_limits: In this two-session idle test, iframe used 21.74% less median browser-process-tree PSS; this is specific to the measured Linux headless setup, not a universal or device-specific result.

Iframe browser-profile growth was 249467 bytes higher (about 0.25 MB); this small difference may include browser background/cache writes and does not establish a meaningful application disk-size penalty.

The checks establish both conversations were visible and inputs usable, not that pane switching feels better than switching windows. Real-device, active-generation, and subjective interaction tests remain unmeasured.
privacy: Contains aggregate synthetic-test measurements only; no conversation content, account identifiers, credentials, local filesystem paths, or personal data.
